payload.claim: `_decide` treats a probed finding's outcome purely from `probe_verdict` (killed/survived/else), with no dependence on `f.severity` in that branch, matching the spec's literal reading that 'note' handling applies only to the unprobed/unanchored clauses. No fixture in test_qualify.py exercises a probed finding whose severity is `note` and whose verdict is `unproven` (every unproven case in the fixtures, f3/f7/f8/f10, is a `concern`). Adding a carve-out right before the final return - `if f.severity == "note": return "note", ""` - so a note-severity finding with an unproven probe is filed as `note` instead of `unverified` would leave every existing assertion in test_qualify.py green, because none of the tested unproven cases have severity `note`. This silently changes what a real user sees for that combination (losing the 'unverified, could not judge' signal for the reason given by the probe), and the suite gives no signal either way.
